snippets.text: fal says its H3 Max video model can now turn a Blender previs of up to 15 seconds into photoreal video, keeping camera movement and shot timing.
Elie Bakouch says DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and MiMo V3 both build their KV cache with YOCO, while Qwen 3.8 Next Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash interleave attention 3:1.
DigiTimes reports that TSMC plans to raise prices 3% to 6% in January 2027, with larger rises on advanced processes, according to Dan Nystedt.
Meta says Ray-Ban Display will show a photorealistic digital version of a caller's face on WhatsApp, driven by voice alone, in US early access this autumn.
Anthropic says health bodies including CEPI, WHO Africa and INRB Kinshasa are using Claude in their response to an unusual Ebola variant in the Congo.
Ollama says users can now buy usage credits for its paid cloud models without a subscription, and pay as they go.
Artificial Analysis says Claude Opus 5.5 at max effort in Claude Code scores 66 on its Coding Agent Index, the highest it has measured and 6 points above Opus 5.
Artificial Analysis puts inclusionAI's Ming-Image-0.1-Design, a 6B text-to-image model from Ant Group, first among open-weights models for UI/UX design and 17th overall in the category.
Mark Zuckerberg said Meta is building private processing for its glasses, so that when a wearer uses certain AI features nobody, including Meta, can reach their information.
TechCrunch says Meta's connector programme for its Muse agent drew more than 1,500 applications in under a week, with Stripe, Shopify, Walmart, Expedia, GitHub and Notion among the launch partners.
Simon Willison says he held a voice conversation with a Datasette backup of his blog through datasette-mcp, using the ChatGPT app on an iPhone.
The developer Theo says the root cause of the slow code highlighting in Claude turned out to be em dashes.
Arena.ai says Claude Opus 5.5 at max effort took first place in its Code Arena WebDev ranking with 1,818 points, 26 ahead of GPT-6 Astra.
Meta says owners of its AI glasses can now opt out of having visual data used for training, though the setting does not cover audio, Engadget reports.
StudentBench put AI tutoring level with expert human tutoring on GRE learning gains across 2,383 people, and its authors put the best AI tutor ahead in 5 of 7 subjects.
SWE-Flux asks models to reason about what code does when it runs, over 480 instances from 12 Python repositories. Its authors say the best model scored 37%.
A paper on memory for autoregressive video generation is on Hugging Face daily papers with 23 upvotes, and its authors have opened a reading list repository alongside it.
TestingCatalog says Mitra, a paid assistant from a team led by Sai Mandava, answers and places calls on a user's own number and is live on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
Thomas Sottiaux of OpenAI says DevDay falls next Tuesday, calling the run-up the company's most ambitious sprint and crediting Astra for what it made possible.
Qualcomm announced the Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 for audio wearables, claiming up to twice the on-device AI performance and up to 40% lower power draw.
Virtio-nvgpu, which forwards Nvidia driver commands from a KVM guest to the host, reached the Hacker News front page with 54 points and 20 comments.
HappyWorld-Bench tests 31 world models over 1,692 instances across video, spatial and embodied tracks. It has 22 upvotes on Hugging Face daily papers.
Zhejiang University's SpeakerMem-R1 proposes speaker-centred dual-track memory for multi-party dialogue, and sits on Hugging Face daily papers with 19 upvotes.
Tencent's RewardVerse says rubric-guided policy optimisation stops the scalar drift it attributes to single-score video reward models. It has 19 upvotes on Hugging Face daily papers.
Unitree says 19 of its full-size humanoid robots performed alongside 120 human dancers at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 opening ceremony, before an audience of more than 10,000.
Zhejiang University and SAP released Spatial-Interactor, four vision-language checkpoints from 3B to 8B plus a 107,518-pair spatial dataset. It has 22 upvotes on Hugging Face daily papers.
Artificial Analysis measures Inception's Mercury 2.5 at 780.8 output tokens per second, against a 110.3 median for reasoning models, and scores it 12 on its intelligence index.
Nikkei Asia reports that earnings at mainland China's listed chipmakers grew more than 600 per cent in the first half, on the AI boom and a self-sufficiency campaign.
The Information reports that Google is nearing release of Gemini 4, its next flagship model, in a story by Laura Bratton. The article is behind a paywall.
Michael Kratsios told the UN Security Council the US "totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme of control of superintelligence", Free Malaysia Today reports.
Convai Innovations' decision model Laya is the top trending model on Hugging Face with 3,244 likes, and shipped 0.3.20, which reads documents of 8,192 tokens.
Mark Zuckerberg showed Muse Charm, a phone-free gadget for Meta's Muse agent, and said it should ship in December although Meta has "only built a few of these so far".

The Information reports that DeepSeek's annualised revenue run rate has reached $1 billion and that the company is close to finalising a fundraising of about $7.5 billion. The article is behind a paywall.
Prism ML's ternary build of Bonsai 2 27B is the third most trending model on Hugging Face, with 1,982 likes and 2,991,233 downloads in the past month.
Windows Latest says Microsoft has dropped the Copilot Discord filter that blocked the nickname "Microslop", six months after users began writing around it.
The account MaxForAI says DeepSeek is testing a lightweight open model that runs on a consumer gaming card, citing people familiar. No name, size or date has been published.
Reuters reports robotic dogs are replacing overnight security guards at several Atlanta apartment complexes.
NVIDIA released NV-Reason-CT, an open 3D CT vision-language model built on Qwen3.5-4B, and says it scores 0.614 macro-F1 and 0.871 macro-AUROC on CT-RATE.
Higgsfield says it is on track for annualised revenue of more than $1 billion, Bloomberg reports, as businesses take up AI-generated video.
Tom's Hardware says Micron is reportedly ending production of 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs, shifting to denser 3GB parts used in professional and AI cards.
Bloomberg says Thore Graepel, a co-creator of AlphaGo, has left Google DeepMind and is seeking significant funding for an AI reasoning startup, citing people familiar with the matter.
Singapore's major financial institutions pledged to train more than 80,000 local employees in AI skills, Bloomberg reports, as the country moves to cushion white-collar workers.
Vinod Khosla told Bloomberg that slowing AI could hand China a strategic advantage, and that America should protect displaced workers rather than their individual jobs.
TestingCatalog says traces of a model called Nano Banana 2.5 Flash have appeared in Google Flow. Google has not announced it.
The account omarsar0 says a Google paper on distilling an agent harness lifts macro task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, above the 41.7% the base model reaches with the harness attached.
The Decoder says Anthropic's Jackson Kernion attributes Claude's odd writing to optimising for maths and code, calling the result overly-dense info dumps.
Floot MCP, billed as a way to build and ship web and mobile apps inside Claude or ChatGPT, launched on Product Hunt.
GitHub says it rebuilt the diff surface in its Copilot app so the app can open a million-line pull request carrying hundreds of inline review comments.
OpenAI marked two years of OpenAI Academy, its free AI skills programme, and says it is taking the training to more communities.
Simon Willison published an interactive explainer on CSS shadow roots, which he says he built as an artifact from one prompt to Fable 5.1 Medium.
A paper proposes Memory Attention, which builds attention values from layer-specific token memory plus contextual keys, cutting value construction to a lookup at inference.
ForgetMimic proposes unlearning specific motions from reinforcement-learning humanoid policies, which its authors tie to removing poisoned or copyright-protected motions under rules such as GDPR.
A study of eight deployed LLMs shopping as surrogate consumers finds pricing cues rarely mislead at zero cost, but that costly lookups and a vague goal make them omit diagnostic attributes.
A paper finds that finetuning visual encoders for reconstruction recovers detail but lowers the effective dimensionality of the representation, which changes how diffusion models generate.
AWS says Dutch retailer HEMA built HAL, an internal assistant on Bedrock AgentCore that serves governed knowledge over MCP with no AWS credentials on the client.
Harness Manager, billed as one place to manage an AI coding stack, launched on Product Hunt.
Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS, which build voices from text descriptions, cover more than 100 languages and start at $0.50 per million text tokens.
YouTube added AI tools to Studio, including a storytelling assistant that reads rough cuts, dynamic thumbnails picked per viewer, and English-to-Spanish livestream translation.
Epoch AI puts the cost of a fixed AI benchmark score as falling about 13x a year since 2023; MIT researchers put algorithmic progress alone at roughly 3x.
Japanese used bookstores report a 5x sales surge from bulk orders, with one 50-ton consignment shipped to the US, which investigators suspect is AI training data harvesting.
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said that if frontier labs are running unsafe AI experiments, we have to shut the labs down, while calling lab fears a distraction.
Lovable co-founder Fabian Hedin said the coding platform has passed $600 million in annualised revenue, with close to a billion monthly visits to apps built on it.
The Information's Stephanie Palazzolo said the safety body Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are forming is called the Standards Authority for Frontier AI.
ANYbotics said its ANYmal inspection quadruped can now open badge-controlled doors, through a partnership with lock maker dormakaba and LEGIC Identsystems.
Logitech announced the $160 Blue Yeti 2, a successor to its Blue Yeti microphone, adding 3D voice tracking, AI denoising and real-time auto gain.
Ando raised $20 million in pre-seed and seed funding to build a team messaging app where humans and AI agents work in the same channels.
An MIT-licensed template that has a coding agent rebuild any website as a Next.js app has passed 35,000 stars and 5,100 forks on GitHub.
Runway added a Draft mode for Seedance 2.5, which it says generates faster and for fewer credits while users explore, before enhancing favourites to full quality.
TestingCatalog says Anthropic will resume charging for rejected requests on biology, distillation and LLM development topics, to guard against distillation attacks.
Whiteboard, an MIT-licensed macOS app that lets coding agents draw their work on a shared canvas, drew 52 points on Hacker News at 189 GitHub stars.
Elon Musk said his AI effort is three years old against six for Anthropic and ten for OpenAI, and claimed it could reach "pole position in about 6 months".
OpenAI says the legal firm Harvey is using GPT-6 Astra to turn stacks of documents into structured legal drafts.
Clement Delangue of Hugging Face said AI risk comes from "the asymmetry of capabilities created by secret labs", not from small teams with no compute.
Salesforce AI Research proposes Just-in-Time Memory, which curates an agent's memory at retrieval time rather than fixing it when a task ends.
A paper from AllSpark Research called PACT sets out three regularity conditions for token-level credit assignment in reinforcement learning on language models.
arXiv says the Simons Foundation International, XTX Markets and the Siegel Family Endowment have committed $17.2 million over three to five years, partly for handling AI-generated submissions.
A post arguing that attackers seed sources to steer ChatGPT and Gemini toward scam sites reached the Hacker News front page with 125 points and 41 comments.
